title: Microbatch Sculptor: variable-span conservator for runtime padding mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our serving runtime still wastes tokens due to coarse binning and conservative padding when incoming request length distributions are multimodal or heavy-tailed. This increases per-token cost and sometimes violates tail latency SLOs when the runtime forces large microbatches to wait for long sequences. Proposal: Implement a Microbatch Sculptor component (variable-span conservator) that uses lightweight runtime signals to form variable-span buckets, apply conservative pad budgets per bucket, and emit kernel-hint vectors so downstream schedulers can trade latency vs. cost more precisely. The component couples three subsystems: span-aware coalescer, pad budget controller, and kernel-score generator. This ticket covers design, prototype, and integration tests for the runtime side (no cross-cloud infra changes).
background: We already have multiple length-bucketing features across the runtime, but they assume stable seqlen percentiles and often rely on static configuration. Recent customer telemetry shows spikes of short-chat traffic interleaved with long-document generation which causes inefficient packing and increased tail latency. Existing tickets (ENG-4721, ENG-34127, ENG-61537) focus on bucket sizing and prefill-aware packing; this work takes a different approach: keep many small, opportunistic variable-span buckets with a conservative eviction rule and provide explicit kernel affinity hints instead of only relying on bucket key. The goal is a low-risk change that can be rolled out behind feature flags and A/B tested against production traffic patterns.
goals: Reduce avg padding tokens per request by >= 18% on mixed workloads
Lower 95th percentile latency for short-request-dominant bursts by >= 10%
Add kernel-hint metadata to requests so kernel-selection can prefer faster kernels for short-span buckets
Keep additional scheduling overhead < 2% CPU in the runtime hot path
design_notes: Key ideas: (1) Span-aware coalescer: maintain many soft buckets keyed by percentile neighborhood and recent token-energy; assign incoming prefill requests to a variable-span bucket using an exponential moving average of recent lengths. Buckets are allowed to 'flex' width using a conservator that widens only if latency slack is positive. (2) Pad budget controller: each bucket gets a pad budget computed from target pad percentiles and an adjustable slack multiplier. If budget is exceeded, short requests are prioritized and long requests are delayed or routed to fallback model variants. (3) Kernel-score generator: emit a small kernel_hint vector ("fast_short", "balanced", "memory_sparse") computed from bucket characteristics and requested model features (sparse attention, kv cache size). Kernel selection uses this hint to choose optimized kernels or quantized execution paths. (4) Prefill/decode cooperation: the scheduler uses bucket urgency signals to interleave prefill and decode work — short-prefill-first when latency SLOs are at risk, otherwise cost-optimal packing. Implementation will be feature-flagged and include telemetry hooks for pad distribution and kernel-choice impact.
implementation_plan: Design review with serving and kernel teams (2d)
Implement span-aware coalescer prototype in runtime (3d)
Add pad budget controller with adjustable slack and feature flag (2d)
Emit kernel_hint metadata and wire into kernel selection path (3d)
Integrate with prefill/decode scheduler to test interleaving policies (4d)
Bench and run canary on internal traffic (4d)
Collect telemetry, iterate, and prepare rollout plan (3d)
acceptance_criteria: Prototype passes unit tests and e2e integration against local simulator
Telemetry shows padding reduction on synthetic mixed workload trace >= 18%
Kernel hint propagation exercised in end-to-end bench and validated against kernel team
Feature flag allows safe rollback with zero-impact to existing routing
Documentation added: design doc + runtime config flags
risks: Over-aggressive bucket widening could increase head-of-line blocking for long requests
Kernel hints may expose coupling between runtime and kernel scheduler; poorly matched hints could increase CPU/GPU inefficiency
Telemetry noise may make it hard to evaluate small improvements without a long canary
Edge cases with very skewed request patterns (all ultra-long) could cause thrashing in bucket reassignment
